title: Compiler Options and Toolchains
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of compiler options and toolchains using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates compiler options and toolchains.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Compiler Options and Toolchains** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands. Use the subtopics—Kotlin Compiler Options, JVM Toolchains and Target Compatibility, Reproducible Build Configuration—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.title: Kotlin Compiler Options
items.text: Kotlin Compiler Options is one part of compiler options and toolchains. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: JVM Toolchains and Target Compatibility
items.text: JVM Toolchains and Target Compatibility means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Reproducible Build Configuration
items.text: Reproducible Build Configuration is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Compiler Options and Toolchains removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
